rationale: Check round against the fix-up diff: backend commits 4367502fe (CR-001, CR-002, CR-003) and 461ca1ae4 (test fix for CR-003's new call site); frontend commits 8b4d81b11 (CR-004 through CR-010) and 2faef9c2f (the 12 previously-deferred, non-blocking cleanup findings, addressed after user request). All 10 prior blocking findings verified resolved: each fix was re-read in place, and where a fix touched test-observable behavior (CR-004's copy change, CR-005's throw path) the specific test file was re-run and confirmed passing. Full-repo verification then run for final confidence: npx tsc --noEmit and eslint clean on the whole frontend src tree; ruff check + format clean on all changed backend files; the full backend router/service/workflow-assistant test files (178 tests) pass; the full frontend unit suite (6224 tests) passes except tests in 4-5 files confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this diff, none of it touched by this diff: Windows path-separator and CRLF platform bugs in modalSurfaces.guard.test.ts, a2ui/manifest.test.ts and check_license_headers.test.js (deterministic, reproduce standalone), plus test-isolation flakes in Popup.test.tsx and NewWorkflowPage.test.tsx that pass standalone and appear/disappear between full-suite runs depending on run order (both confirmed passing in isolation; NewWorkflowPage passed in the final full run, failed in the prior one). The final full run: 613/617 files, 6220/6224 tests passed, 1 skipped, 3 failed (the 3 deterministic platform bugs). No new high-risk issue was introduced by the fix-up diff itself. ADDENDUM (commit 151bbedc0, after this round's original approval): while writing the companion codemie-sdk regression tests, the user asked whether an item from the pre-review notes ('project admins lost budget distribution, EPMCDME-13962 regression') should be in scope. Re-investigation found it was a live, currently-broken regression, not a stale note — confirmed against the test-harness's own EPMCDME-13962 UI test, which requires the exact control this bug removed. Recorded as CR-011 below, fixed, and re-verified. ADDENDUM 2 (second independent review, 2026-09-25): a fresh pass over the whole feature found eight more in-scope issues, recorded as CR-012..CR-019 and fixed. Four further items were judged outside this story's acceptance criteria by the user and deferred as follow-up candidates, not fixed here: enforcing project model settings in the LiteLLM proxy used by the CLI/IDE, optimistic concurrency (revision + 409) on the settings PUT, an activity-log audit trail for settings changes, and a cache for per-request settings reads.

findings.title: Project admins lost budget distribution access (EPMCDME-13962 regression)
findings.problem: canManageBudgets was computed as isBudgetManagementEnabled && isMaintainer only. ProjectBudgetsSection still received the correct 3-tier `access` prop (full/distribution/view) but a second `mode` prop, always derived from this maintainer-only boolean, unconditionally overrode it inside the component.
findings.impact: A platform admin or project admin (the 'distribution' tier from EPMCDME-13962 restore an existing budget's member split, not create/reset/rebalance/delete it) saw no budget control at all, on Overview or the Budgets tab — not reduced capability, none. Confirmed as a live regression against test-harness's own test_project_admin_updates_distribution_via_ui (EPMCDME-13962 TC-02), which requires this control for a project-admin persona.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `mode` prop; drive ProjectBudgetManagementControl from `access` alone, restoring the original hasFullAccess/isDistributionOnly split (including UnifiedProjectBudgetModal's distributionOnly flag, which had been disconnected).

findings.title: Project restrictions could be bypassed through shared or marketplace assistants
findings.problem: Runtime resolution applied the policy of assistant.project (the owning project), not the caller's.
findings.impact: A member of a restricted project reached hidden models by chatting with an assistant owned by an unrestricted project (AC 3, AC 5).
findings.recommendation: Govern members by the entity's project and non-members by every restricting project they belong to (policy_for).

findings.title: Chat model picker empty for marketplace assistants (regression from the CR-002 fix)
findings.problem: GET /v1/llm_models?project= returned 403 to non-members; the chat picker requests the assistant owner's project.
findings.impact: Conversations with an assistant from another project showed no selectable model.
findings.recommendation: Answer non-members with their own policy; the owner project's settings are neither applied nor revealed.

findings.title: Workflow custom nodes bypassed project model settings
findings.problem: custom_node.model went straight to get_llm_by_credentials; workflow save never validated models.
findings.impact: A workflow YAML could run any model regardless of the project's restrictions (AC 5 names workflows).
findings.recommendation: Resolve the node model through resolve_runtime_model; reject hidden assistant/custom-node models on workflow create and update.

findings.title: Saving model settings could be blocked by a model removed from the catalog
findings.problem: validate() rejected every name missing from the catalog, including names already stored (e.g. in other members' overrides).
findings.impact: After a model left the platform config, every later save of the project failed with 422 until each stale reference was found by hand.
findings.recommendation: Prune previously stored names that left the catalog before validating; still reject newly introduced unknown names.

findings.title: Settings leaving no model available passed validation
findings.problem: An allow list of only premium models plus hide_premium_models, or an override disabling a member's last model, saved successfully.
findings.impact: Every chat for the project (or member) then failed at runtime with 403.
findings.recommendation: Reject such settings with 422; the Models tab now says 'Enable at least one model that is not hidden'.

findings.title: Model fallback was invisible to the user
findings.problem: The chat selector showed a now-hidden chat model as 'Default' while the backend ran another model; LLMSelector's reset warning cleared itself in the same render it was raised.
findings.impact: Users were never told their selected model had been replaced.
findings.recommendation: Chat: announce and clear a hidden chat model once. LLMSelector: keep the warning while the reset value is shown.

findings.title: No unit tests for the new backend and frontend code
findings.problem: Only the SDK/test-harness API tests (which need a live server) covered the feature.
findings.impact: Sonar new-code coverage would block the MR and regressions would go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add backend service/router/node/assignment tests and frontend store/hook/helper/component tests.

findings.title: Member model overrides survived removal from the project
findings.problem: Removing a member left their entry in member_overrides.
findings.impact: A re-added member silently regained old restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Drop the member's override on single and bulk removal.
